extracted.intended_audience: PD/PIs, PD/PI delegates, Signing Officials, AOs, SOs, and grants administrators preparing and submitting NIH RPPRs via eRA Commons
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and standards for preparing, editing, validating, routing, and submitting Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) in eRA Commons, including formatting, file handling, inclusion enrollment reporting, multi-project handling, and role-based actions. Applies to annual, Interim, and Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not flatten Common Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should note that Common Forms (Biosketch and Current & Pending (Other) Support Forms) in most cases should NOT be flattened, to retain signature validations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid flattening these forms because signature validations are retained when not flattened. This is an explicit preference in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF attachments must be submitted as individual files
rubrics_metrics.description: The PDF format is used to preserve document formatting. All PDF attachments must be submitted as individual files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use software 'Bundling' or 'Portfolio' features to combine multiple PDFs into a single file; eRA systems cannot support bundling and use of these features may result in delays in agency acceptance of the progress report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid paginated PDF files
rubrics_metrics.description: Paginated PDF files are also discouraged since they can interfere with system pagination of the entire RPPR document upon submission to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit paginated PDFs that embed their own page numbers or pagination metadata that may conflict with eRA Commons system pagination.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Save all files with descriptive file names of 50 characters or less and be sure to only use standard characters in file names: A through Z, a through z, 0 through 9, and underscore (_). Do not use any special characters or spacing in the file name, and for word separation use an underscore (e.g., My_Attached_File.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid characters such as &, -, *, %, /, and #. Keep names descriptive but concise (≤50 chars). Use underscore instead of spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface, font color, size, and density requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an Arial, Helvetica, Palatino Linotype, or Georgia typeface, a black font color, and a font size of 11 points or larger. (A Symbol font may be used to insert Greek letters or special characters; the font size requirement still applies.) Type density, including characters and spaces, must be no more than 15 characters per inch. Type may be no more than six lines per inch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure allowed fonts and black color; if using Symbol font for special characters maintain minimum size. Check type density and line spacing to meet numeric limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper size and margins
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard paper size (8 ½" x 11). Use at least one-half inch margins (top, bottom, left, and right) for all pages. No information should appear in the margins, including the PD/PI’s name and page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure no header/footer or identifying info is placed in the margins; adhere to 0.5" minimum margins on all sides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and style expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use English and avoid jargon. Abbreviations and language that may not be known to the broader scientific community should be avoided unless clearly defined. Internet Web site addresses (URLs) should not be used unless otherwise specified in the RPPR instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for a broad scientific audience; define any necessary abbreviations and avoid casual use of URLs unless instructions explicitly permit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save before leaving screens
rubrics_metrics.description: Users may work on various sections in any order; however, it is important to click the Save button in the navigation bar before leaving a screen in order to retain data entered on that screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigating away from any page on the RPPR without selecting Save results in the loss of any information entered prior to the last save. Always click Save before moving between sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text boxes have character limits and show remaining characters
rubrics_metrics.description: All text boxes on the RPPR have character limits. The number of characters available is reflected beneath each text box as characters are entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the remaining character count while typing; plan content to fit within limits or use attachments where allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing saved responses warns and deletes previous response
rubrics_metrics.description: While an RPPR is in Work In Progress status, answers may be changed. A warning message displays: 'The entered/uploaded response will be deleted. Do you wish to continue?' Choosing Continue deletes the previous response, removes any attachments, and disables the relevant fields associated with the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When altering previously saved responses, be aware that attachments and associated data may be removed; choose Cancel to preserve existing content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may initiate an RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the PD/PI or the PD/PI delegate may initiate an RPPR. When there are multiple PIs (MPI), only the Contact PI or the PD/PI delegate of the Contact PI may initiate the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiation access is role-limited. Use the RPPR module or Status links as described to initiate. If initiation fails, business rules validations may display errors/warnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year RPPR initiation restrictions and link availability
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-year funded awards, the link will display as RPPR Year <X>. The link for a multi-year funded award is available two months prior to the RPPR due date for the current reporting period and remains available until the RPPR is submitted. You are prevented from initiating a reporting year’s progress report until the progress report(s) of the previous year(s) has been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan ahead for initiation windows; do not expect to initiate a later-year RPPR until earlier years are submitted. AHRQ may have different implementation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation validation may block progress until profile info completed
rubrics_metrics.description: An RPPR can be initiated even if required information in the Personal Profile and Institution Profile sections is missing. If any of this information is incorrect or missing, a prompt will appear to correct/complete the information after initiating the report. Processing may continue on the RPPR without making the corrections; however, the RPPR will not pass validations for submission to the agency until the errors are corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may begin editing before fixing profile issues, but final validations for submission will fail until profile errors/warnings are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR status values
rubrics_metrics.description: Status: The current state of the progress report. Possible values are as follows: Not Started, PD/PI Work in Progress, Reviewer Work in Progress, and Submitted to Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the RPPR status on the RPPR Menu screen to know what actions are available and the current reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role- and status-dependent actions under the three-dot ellipsis menu
rubrics_metrics.description: After an RPPR is initiated, several actions appear under the three-dot ellipses icon next to Award Number. Available actions vary depending on the status of the RPPR and/or the limitations of the current user’s role. Possible actions include: Edit RPPR; View RPPR as PDF; Check for Errors; View Routing History; Route to Next Reviewer; Recall; Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access rules by action: Edit RPPR available to PD/PIs or delegates when current reviewer, AOs/SOs when current reviewer; View RPPR as PDF available in WIP or Submitted; Check for Errors available to any user with access in WIP; Route to Next Reviewer only by current reviewer (PD/PI delegate cannot route); Recall available to last reviewer and under special cases to SOs/PD/PIs; Submit available to SO when SO is current reviewer and to PD/PI when delegated Progress Report authority. Buttons/options shown are context-sensitive (only those possible appear).

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing RPPR as PDF shows Draft until submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission to the awarding agency, the system will generate a PDF of the progress report. View RPPR as PDF opens the RPPR report in PDF format, as it will be seen by the agency. Until the RPPR is submitted to agency, the PDF report shows a status of Draft and a blank submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the View PDF to preview the assembled report exactly as the agency will see it; do not assume the Draft PDF represents a submitted report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing, recall, and submit workflow constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR can be routed to the next reviewer. A PD/PI delegate cannot route an RPPR to the next reviewer. Recall resets the user as the current reviewer and is available for reports with WIP; Signing Officials and PD/PIs can recall an RPPR even if they are not the last reviewer whenever it has a status of Reviewer Work in Progress. Only a signing official (SO) can submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand delegation limits: routing and submission are controlled by reviewer role and delegation; use Recall to retrieve misrouted reports; only SOs perform final submission unless PD/PI has delegated submit authority as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final RPPR and Interim RPPR timing and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Final Research Performance Progress Report (Final RPPR) is required for any grant that has ended and any grant that is not to be extended through award of a new competitive segment. The report is due within 120 days of the end of the project period. If the recipient organization has submitted a renewal application on or before the date by which a Final RPPR would be required, an Interim RPPR via eRA Commons is required for submission of a Competing Renewal application (Type 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim RPPR and Final RPPR are identical in process and information required; differences from the annual RPPR are noted (see next metric). Interim RPPR link availability differs (made available to the SO when eligible for renewal submission).

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences between Interim/Final RPPR and annual RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences between Interim/Final RPPR and the annual RPPR are few: In the Interim/Final RPPR, only Section D.1 is required in the Participants section; Sections F: Changes and H: Budget are not part of the Interim/Final RPPR; Section I: Outcomes is required for both the Interim/Final RPPR (Outcomes does not appear in the system for the annual RPPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow component-specific instructions when preparing Interim or Final RPPRs; be aware required sections differ from annual submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim RPPR handling if renewal outcome changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are awarded the renewal, the Interim RPPR will be treated as your annual RPPR and no other progress reporting will be needed for that segment. If the application is NOT awarded, then the Interim RPPR will be accepted as the Final RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit duplicate reports for the same period; the Interim RPPR may substitute depending on renewal outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR components must be reported and can be added/deleted
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project awards, each component must be reported in the RPPR. To add an individual component: click Add Component -> New Component and enter title/type. Individual components can be removed by selecting Delete from the component’s menu; the component is deleted immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important: Deleting a component permanently removes all data related to that component — including all budget data — and this data cannot be recovered once deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table tools and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Built-in table tools let you work with data in tables: Filter (instant filtering with highlighted matches), Sorting Columns (click headers to sort ascending/descending), Download/Print Tool (export table data to Excel or PDF), Rows-Per-Page Tool, and Search Results Navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these tools to manage long lists; downloaded exports include data from all columns even if not visible on screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) editing workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: To update inclusion enrollment data, select the Human Subjects link from question G.4 of section G. The Human Subjects link takes you to the Application Information screen -> HSCT Post Submission tab -> Study Record(s) screen. Click View to inspect study records and Edit to change inclusion enrollment data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important: Before selecting the Human Subjects link, click Save on the RPPR to save all of your work in Section G — failure to do so will result in loss of data on your report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Enrollment Report fields
rubrics_metrics.description: The Inclusion Enrollment Report contains fields including: Using an Existing Dataset or Resource (Yes/No), Enrollment Location Type (Domestic/Foreign), Enrollment Country(ies), Enrollment Location(s), and Comments (optional cumulative enrollment comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the application guide for details on expected content for each field; Comments may be pre-populated when editing an existing IER.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative and planned inclusion tables behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The cumulative enrollment table includes racial categories along the left side of the table and ethnic categories, divided by sex, along the top of the table. Individual enrollment count cells are editable and set to zero by default for a new IER; totals are calculated by HSS and are not editable. The cumulative inclusion table includes fields for entering Unknown/Not Reported race, ethnicity, and sex data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing, update individual cells as necessary; totals auto-calculate so do not attempt to modify totals directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two methods to populate cumulative inclusion data
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to edit the existing Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER) data for Cumulative (Actual) counts: (1) update the cells online in the existing report itself; (2) download a template for entering participant-level data (CSV), fill it, and upload the spreadsheet which will populate the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Buttons available: Download Participant Level Data Template; Upload Participant Level Data Attachment; Download Current Participant Level Data; Remove Current Participant Level Data. Use the template CSV format when uploading to ensure correct ingestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Save and release lock when editing IER
rubrics_metrics.description: Update the values in the individual enrollment count cells as necessary, and select the Save and Release Lock button. To leave the form without saving any changes, select the Cancel and Release Lock button instead. Saving and canceling both return you to the Study Record(s) screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Save and Release Lock to commit changes; use Cancel and Release Lock to exit without saving while releasing edit lock so others can edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy requiring individual-level participant data for some RPPRs
rubrics_metrics.description: POLICY: Individual-level participant data on sex, race, ethnicity and age at enrollment is required in progress reports for competitive applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2019 (See NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-18-116). Inclusion data for subsequent RPPRs must be provided using the file upload option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For competitive applications with due dates on/after Jan 25, 2019, prepare participant-level data and use CSV upload for subsequent RPPRs as required by policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission blocked if inclusion monitoring required and no IERs exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If inclusion monitoring is required and no IERs exist, RPPR system will NOT allow the submission of the progress report without IER(s) for the current FY. For past FYs (when the progress report is late), a standard message is displayed instead of an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must create and save a new IER (Add New Inclusion Enrollment Report) to resolve the error and permit submission. Upon saving a new IER, planned and cumulative data objects are created and assigned a unique IER #.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit a new planned inclusion record
rubrics_metrics.description: From the Study Record(s) screen, select the Add New Inclusion Enrollment Report to create a new IER. If no study records exist, first add a study record using instructions in the online help.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After creating a new IER and saving, planned inclusion data and cumulative fields (initialized to zeros) are created; ensure you complete or upload participant-level data as required and Save and Release Lock.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR Budget Form (H.1) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: To add a budget, choose an option from the drop-down list and click the Add Budget button. The added budget type appears in the first table; click the budget’s three-dot ellipsis menu and select Edit to open the form for editing. Most awards now use the SF424 R&R budget form. However, training awards may use the SF424 and/or the PHS 398 training budget. The PHS Additional Indirect Costs budget form is available as an optional form for the Overall component of a multi-project award with multiple organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure which budget form to use, contact the Grants Management Specialist assigned to your grant. Note: After deleting a budget form, be sure to save the RPPR before navigating away.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget types list and deletion
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget types include: SF 424 Research & Related Budget form; PHS 398 Training Budget; PHS Additional Indirect Costs form. Budget types can be deleted by clicking the budget’s three-dot ellipsis icon and selecting Delete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After deleting a budget form, save the RPPR to persist changes. Deletion may remove data that cannot be recovered unless previously saved elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not close the browser or use the back button when returning from external links
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that a link to a site outside the RPPR (e.g., U.S. Select Agency Registry in F.3.d, or the NIH human embryonic stem cell Registry in G.6) opens a site in a new browser window. You must close that window to return to the RPPR. Do not close the browser or use the browser’s back button.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the new window and close it when finished; using browser back/close may disrupt the RPPR session and lead to data loss or navigation issues.
